## TL;DR

Completed the numeric enum settings fix after review surfaced five omitted resource settings. A shared key list now drives both API validation and numeric TOML persistence for all nine numeric selects. Table-driven API coverage verifies number and string payloads reload as numbers, and a CLI integration test exercises `repoos config set maxConcurrentAgents 4`. The scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The first implementation focused on the four keys already converted to numbers in the config PATCH route. Review correctly pointed out that five resource settings also have numeric runtime types even though their select options are strings: `heavySlots`, `vitest.maxWorkers`, `localChecks.maxConcurrent`, `playwright.workers`, and `playwright.maxConcurrent`. Their parsers and consumers expect numeric values, so accepting a dropdown string without converting it would serialize a quoted TOML string that reload ignores.

I centralized all nine settings in `NUMERIC_SELECT_CONFIG_KEYS` in core config. The route uses this set to normalize incoming values for option comparison and to convert accepted values to numbers before writing. That keeps validation and persistence tied to the same declaration. The special `closeOut.timeoutMs` handling remains on its own path because it accepts whole numbers outside its preset options.

The table-driven tests assert the data rows match the shared key tuple, verify each enum has the expected option, and send both numeric and string forms through the PATCH handler. Each case reloads the TOML and checks the setting at its root or nested path is the expected number; this avoids relying only on substring matching. A separate integration case runs `config set maxConcurrentAgents 4` against a test server and checks both the loaded value and persisted TOML integer.

## Approaches tried

I considered changing schema option values to numbers, but the dropdowns submit strings and that would change UI-facing metadata. Instead, API validation compares a canonical string for the numeric-select subset, while the existing runtime semantics are preserved by numeric conversion before persistence. I also considered keeping a separate list in the route for its conversion step; the shared constant avoids repeating the same classification in validation and persistence.

Review also highlighted that the initial test’s TOML substring assertion could pass on an unrelated nested key. I replaced that as the primary check with a fresh `loadConfig()` read and kept a negative assertion that the TOML leaf is not quoted.

## Challenges and blockers

No implementation blockers remain. The expanded config change selected 559 changed-path test files on remote validation, substantially more than the earlier pass. The remote build and test gate completed successfully; rendered contrast and UI smoke passed as well. Local format, lint, build, contrast, and UI smoke guards all passed. The final check reported no failed steps.

## Key learnings

Select option values reflect the browser control’s wire type, not necessarily the setting’s runtime type. Numeric selects need one source of truth for normalization and serialization, and their regression tests should verify a reload into runtime config. CLI coverage matters separately because `config set` parses numeric arguments into JSON numbers, while the Settings dropdown sends strings; both paths now converge on the same validator and persistence behavior.
